## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Fix "Restore `--wait` as a deprecated alias" before merge: the ADR added in this pull request promises a one-release `--wait` alias with a deprecation warning, but the parser drops `--wait`, so existing invocations now fail.

## Changes
This pull request renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout` in `app/cli.py` and keeps the default of 30. It updates `tests/test_cli.py` to use the new name, adds ADR `docs/adr/007-timeout.md`, and adds a one-line `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Restore `--wait` as a deprecated alias — `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with code 2 ("unrecognized arguments") because only `--timeout` is registered. That contradicts `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5`: "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." No test covers the alias or the warning. — Every existing script that passes `--wait` breaks immediately and gets no deprecation period. — Fix: Register `--wait` with `dest="timeout"` and an action that emits a `DeprecationWarning`, then add a `--wait` case beside `test_explicit_options`.
